review_method: Visual comparison of each sampled question-paper block against the corresponding markscheme pages

sample.strategy: All flagged blocks plus a deterministic cross-paper sample of unflagged blocks

reviews.notes: The Maclaurin substitution and 2-mark boundary match the question paper and markscheme.
The squared-series route and trigonometric-identity alternative both match the markscheme.
The differentiation route and both accepted alternatives are supported by the markscheme.
This is a function graph transformation, not general geometric reasoning.
Odd-function graph reconstruction belongs to function analysis.
The combined block is justified because the two printed answers share the 2-mark allocation.
The markscheme gives one shared method mark across the two limits, so the combined block is appropriate.
The explanation and x-on-y regression calculation share the printed 4-mark allocation.
The task summary had the wrong sign. A dedicated differential-equations topic was also added.
The block method, row-boundary handling, and alternative line method match the markscheme.
The two case-based counting routes and final total match the markscheme.
Both direct extrema timing and half-period methods are valid and correctly summarized.

The task explicitly uses coordinates and perpendicular vectors in three dimensions.
The common argument gap and De Moivre alternative both give n=24 as in the markscheme.
The frequency and mean equations, elimination, and 5-mark boundary are correct.

B=(0,0) follows directly from the previously derived inflection x-coordinate and the curve equation.
